note: Coefficients for business modules. 'literature' coefficients must stay inside their published range ('ranges', checked by the engine and tests); 'labelled_default' are uncalibrated scale or neutral choices with no published range; 'heuristic' are practice values from general business sense. Nothing here comes from any game. Not a forecast.

sources: Cooper & Nakanishi 1988 (MCI: one multiplicative term with its own elasticity per instrument, eq. 2.7)
demand chain ad_elasticity (data/demand_literature.json): Sethuraman, Tellis & Briesch 2011, short-term mean 0.12 (median 0.05), long-term mean 0.24 (median 0.10)

media_weights.why: No published general ranking of local, regional, social and search media; equal weights are the neutral choice until Q2+ data.

sources: Albers, Mantrala & Sridhar 2010, JMR 47(5): mean current-period personal-selling elasticity 0.34, about 0.31 after method-bias correction (506 estimates; abstract verified; dispersion not verified)
Lodish 1971 (call-response curves)
constant-elasticity response as in the meta-analysis

force_reference.why: Scale of the force per market at which the response is (1+1)^e; chosen for the synthetic pack.

sources: direction only: Griffeth, Hom & Gaertner 2000, pay vs turnover rho about -0.09

Sokolova & Sorensen 2021, ILR Review 74(1): median labour-supply elasticity to the firm 1.68 (1.41 direct estimates; working-paper full text); a separation elasticity would need a steady-state conversion, an inference not reported by them

costs (hire_cost, severance_cost).why: The game's sales-force cost rule was not observed.

sources: Arthur, Bennett, Edens & Bell 2003, J. Applied Psychology 88(2): sample-weighted mean d = 0.62 on results criteria (0.60-0.63 across reaction, learning, behaviour, results; abstract verified in the published PDF)
training (training_scale, skill_decay, s.why: d is in standard deviations of performance; turning it into a sales multiplier needs the spread of salesperson performance, which has no published general value. Farrell & Hakstian 2001's '23.1%' could not be verified anywhere and is no longer cited.

web sales (web_force_reference, web_elas.why: The personal-selling meta-analysis (Albers et al. 2010) covers field sales forces; no published elasticity for web or phone salespeople.

sources: Azzi, Battini, Faccio, Persona & Sgarbossa 2014, Int. J. Logistics Management 25(1), literature review quoting Stock & Lambert 1993 (12-34%) and Schonberger & Knod 1997 / Pyke & Cohen 1994 (20-50%) of inventory value per year (introduction verified)
form: Harris 1913

salvage_fraction.why: No published general salvage rate (Cachon & Kok 2007 is about estimating it, not a value).

sources: Dolan 1987 (all-units quantity discounts)
Monahan 1984

discount_tiers.why: No published typical discount magnitudes; tiers chosen for the synthetic pack's production volume.

sources: price response of the demand chain (mean price elasticity -2.62: Bijmolt, van Heerde & Pieters 2005, JMR 42(2); abstract)

perceived_weight, redemption_rate.why: No peer-reviewed redemption or slippage rate found (Lu & Moorthy 2007 and Gilpatric 2009 model rebates without a rate).

lift.why: Content moderates advertising response (direction only); no generalizable magnitude found.

sources: borrowed: Sethuraman, Tellis & Briesch 2011 short-term advertising mean 0.12 (not online-specific)

report_price.why: The game's report prices are unobserved.

sources: Kaplan & Norton 1992, HBR 70(1): four perspectives

weights and references.why: No published weights; the game's ranking formula is unverified.

sources: direction: efficiency wages; Sokolova & Sorensen 2021 (labour supply, not output)
direction: Doucouliagos 1995, ILR Review 49(1) (participation and productivity, 43 studies; abstract)
all.why: No usable coefficient at the depth verified.

sources: 29 U.S.C. 207(a)(1): at least 1.5 x the regular rate (statute, full text)
overtime_premium.why: A legal floor, not the game's rule.

sources: direction: Shepard & Clifton 2000 (abstract); Pencavel 2015 (abstract)

all.why: The game's site options and costs are unobserved.

Scarf 1960, (S,s) optimality (cited)
normal safety stock: Silver, Pyke & Peterson 1998 (textbook)

record_quarters.why: Window of the demand record; cover and z are the player's choices.

priority (production.scheduling).why: The game's allocation rule is unobserved.
